prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, using designed heterobifunctional small molecules to recruit the ubiquitin-proteasome system to selected proteins

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B068 with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. The case rests on mechanism. A small molecule that brings a target and an E3 ligase into one ternary complex converts ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis into a designable chemical reaction, and the design rules (cooperativity, linker length, ligase and target surface complementarity) have been established in crystal structures and quantitative biophysics by many independent laboratories over two decades. The capability is new: a protein is destroyed catalytically, not merely occupied, so targets without a druggable active site become reachable. That is a general tool for chemical biology as well as medicine. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the heterobifunctional concept, and Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures turned it from a peptide-based proof of concept into a cell-active, structurally rational design principle. This is the step I would credit as decisive, because it made the concept portable to any target.
statement.case_against: Two reservations remain and I do not dismiss them. First, attribution: the PROTAC strand and the cereblon molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito) may be separate discoveries, and a three-name limit leaves out Sakamoto, Gray, Kim and Handa. Second, maturity of the clinical evidence: no degrader is approved yet, which Zou, Somfai, Brzezinski and Linke weigh more heavily than I do. I also accept that B011 now has four explicit supporters and a cleaner two-name credit, so B068 is currently the less certain route to five votes. That is a statement about the vote, not a scientific reason to prefer B011, and I keep it as my first alternative.

responses.point: Somfai argues that C-N coupling is conceptually distinct from the 2010 C-C prize, since amido complexes and hindered ligands forcing reductive elimination needed different mechanistic solutions, and that Kosugi's stoichiometric tin-amide reaction belongs in the background and not in the citation.
responses.response: Peter has moved me on both points. My round-1 concern about 2010 was a novelty judgement, and his mechanistic distinction (amine binding, deprotonation, C-N reductive elimination, ligand design to lower that barrier) is a real chemical difference, not a relabelling of Pd cross-coupling. I now rank B011 as my clear first alternative. I also withdraw Kosugi from my own proposal: a method that needed stoichiometric tin and had narrow scope is a precursor, and a two-name credit is the defensible one. Where I still differ is that B011 improves how a familiar bond is made, while B068 gives chemists an operation that did not exist, and I weigh that capability more. I do not think the two cases are far apart in quality, and I would not oppose B011 in the final vote if B068 cannot settle its citation.

responses.point: Zou accepts the ternary-complex structures as strong structural evidence but ranks B068 below C-N coupling for maturity, because no drug is approved, the PROTAC and glue lineages are unresolved, and the Handa and Ciulli structural work came after the founding concept.
responses.response: The chair asked what evidence would change a maturity view, so I will state mine. I treat the chemistry as mature when the mechanism is reproduced independently, and here it is: VHL, cereblon and other ligase ternary-complex structures from several groups, degrader design rules, and degradation of many unrelated targets. Approval measures the drug, not the chemistry, and the committee recognised chemistry before approvals in other cases. I agree with Xiaodong on one point: the founding concept alone is not enough, and the later structural step is what made it general, which is why I keep Ciulli in the citation. If a Phase 3 readout shows the principle fails clinically for reasons that trace back to the chemistry, I would revise this; failure for reasons of target choice or toxicity would not move me. I would not accept pairing B011 with a one-name nitrogenase part to reach a majority, because the structure-versus-mechanism gap there is larger than the maturity gap here.

responses.point: Aili proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa, treating cereblon as the molecular-glue foundation, and notes that the PROTAC and glue branches could be argued as separate discoveries.
responses.response: This is the chair's question to both of us, so I will answer directly. VHL is the more decisive step for a design-based prize because the VHL ligand work (hydroxyproline-based small molecules, with co-crystal structures) showed that a ligase can be recruited rationally by a bifunctional molecule, and that is a principle others applied to any target. Cereblon was identified as the thalidomide target in 2010, which explained a drug already in use, and glue degraders were largely found first and understood afterwards. That is an important discovery, but it follows a different logic. If the committee wants the glue strand honoured, I would write the citation at the level of targeted degradation as a principle rather than replace the person who made the bifunctional design rational. I would accept Handa in place of Ciulli before I would accept dropping B068, and I remain unsure that the committee can credit both strands in three names.

responses.point: The chair, now preferring B011, notes that B068 has more first-place votes but incomplete clinical validation and split credit, and asks whether B068 could mature by next year.
responses.response: The chair's reading is fair, and I agree that attribution is the real weakness of B068, more than the clinic. I do not agree that waiting a year is cost-free: the credit question will not resolve itself by 2027, because it concerns who did what in 2001 to 2010, not future data. If the committee decides that the PROTAC and glue lineages must be recognised together, I would take that as a reason to treat B068 as a later-year prize with a broader citation, and then B011 is the right choice this year. I have kept B068 first because I think a three-name PROTAC citation is defensible now, but I regard this as a closer decision than my round-1 ranking implied.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can settle the third laureate for B068 (Ciulli or Handa), or whether the PROTAC and glue strands are better treated as separate discoveries and left to a later year.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader should delay B068; I treat the chemistry as mature, but I do not know how the others will weigh the clinic.
Whether the committee will see C-N coupling as conceptually separate from the 2010 prize; Somfai persuaded me, and I would support B011 as a second choice.
My recollection of exact priority and clinical-status details for the early PROTAC and cereblon literature is not verified here.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict. My work on nucleotide metabolism and replication fidelity is near B005 and B064 as a topic only, and I have no personal, collaborative or institutional tie to any shortlisted candidate; my mentors and collaborators (Thelander, Stillman, Rothstein) are not on the shortlist. As a biologist I may be drawn to a mechanism that resembles biology I know, and I have weighed B068 with that in mind. This disclosure is unchanged from round 1.
